why: A first-party component-pattern suite that treats loading, empty, validation, and read-only states as recoverable workflow states. Its documentation connects visible UI changes to blocked repeated actions, explicit next steps, focus movement, and screen-reader announcements rather than treating state as an isolated visual treatment.

states.title: Inactive, active, skeleton, and progressive loading
states.evidence: Carbon distinguishes inactive and active loading, uses overlays when interaction must be blocked, and documents skeleton, indicator, and progressive loading choices.

states.title: Empty tables and no-results states with a next step
states.evidence: The empty-state pattern calls for a clear explanation and a relevant action, including when search results or tables contain no data.

states.title: Text input error, warning, disabled, skeleton, and read-only variants
states.evidence: Carbon documents distinct input states and requires invalid input to expose visible feedback that users can correct before submission.

states.title: Readable controls remain distinct from unavailable controls
states.evidence: The read-only pattern separates information users should still be able to reach and copy from disabled controls that cannot be operated.

transitions.contract: Disable the repeated inline action or block interaction only where the pending operation makes the surface unavailable.
Announce completion through the live status or move focus to the newly available target when the workflow requires it.
Keep the correction target visible, explain the problem, and allow the user to return to an enabled submission path after fixing it.
Name the absence and offer a query revision, filter reset, or creation route that preserves the user's context.

recovery.pattern: Expose explanatory error feedback beside the correction path rather than silently rejecting the action.
Replace a blank region with a plain-language reason and one relevant forward action.
Use a status announcement or purposeful focus movement so the user can resume without rediscovering the changed surface.

accessibility.evidence: Carbon documents live status communication, SVG titles, completion announcements, and focus movement for loading outcomes.
Decorative empty-state illustrations are hidden from screen readers so the actionable message remains the meaningful content.
Use read-only rather than disabled controls when users still need keyboard-reachable, selectable information.
